dicas.texto: Você está indo muito bem! Lembre-se: em uma reta numérica, quanto mais à esquerda um número está, menor ele é. O que isso nos diz sobre a distância de cada ponto em relação ao zero?
Observe a posição dos dois pontos que você marcou. Qual deles está mais próximo do número zero na reta numérica?
O ponto que está mais perto do zero representa a menor quantidade. Compare visualmente a distância do ponto 1/4 e do ponto 1/5 até o zero.
Olhe atentamente para a reta: o ponto 1/5 está mais perto do zero ou o ponto 1/4? O que estiver mais perto do zero é o que representa a menor parte lida.

dicas.texto: What does the denominator tell you about the whole novel?
Look at the number below the fraction bar and use that number to divide the interval from 0 to 1.
Levar's fraction is 1/4, so make four equal spaces between 0 and 1.
Enter the number of equal parts named by the denominator of Levar's fraction, then confirm it.
What does the numerator tell you to count on the divided number line?
Start at 0 and count the number of equal intervals named by the numerator.
Because the numerator is 1, choose the first division point after 0.
On the line divided into four equal parts, click the first interval mark to the right of 0.
What does the denominator show about the number of equal parts?
Use the number below the fraction bar to divide the interval from 0 to 1.
Laura's fraction has 5 as its denominator, so create five equal spaces.
Enter the number of equal parts shown by Laura's denominator, then confirm it.
What does the numerator tell you to count from 0?
Start at 0 and count one equal interval on Laura's divided number line.
Since the numerator is 1, choose the first division point after 0.
On the line divided into five equal parts, click the first interval mark to the right of 0.
Which marked point is closer to 0 on the two number lines?
Compare the distances of the two marked fractions from 0 rather than comparing the denominators alone.
Use the positions of the marked points to decide which student's amount is smaller.
Select the student named by the required comparison result, not the option saying the amounts are equal.
Have you compared both marked fractions before finishing?
Review the selected comparison and then use the completion control.
Make sure the selector contains the required student comparison before submitting.
Keep the required comparison selected and press Done to submit the exercise.

exercicio.statement:
Levar and Laura are reading a novel as a class assignment. Use the number line to find out which student has read less of the novel.
Levar has read 1/4 of the novel.
Laura has read 1/5 of the novel.
